title: Room Temp — Weather App
description: A Flutter weather app that goes beyond the forecast: live conditions, hourly and 3-day forecasts and air quality, paired with a physics-based thermal model that estimates the temperature inside your room.
headline: Outdoor weather data, turned into an indoor answer.
overview: Most weather apps stop at the forecast. Room Temp pulls live conditions, forecasts, air quality and UV data, then runs them through a lumped-capacitance thermal model that accounts for room size, sunlight exposure and whether an AC or heater is running, so the number you see is the one that matters inside your room.
architecture: Core, data and presentation layers with Riverpod view-models between the UI and the repository
A request token drops superseded fetches, so rapid city searches never overwrite each other
Pure-Dart thermal model, unit-tested and guarded against NaN and Infinity

features.title: Indoor estimate
features.body: A three-stage thermal model covering thermal lag, solar gain and capacity-limited AC or heating.

features.title: Weather-reactive scenes
features.body: Clear, night, rain, snow, fog and haze scenes, each with legibility-matched text colours.

features.title: Cities & map picker
features.body: GPS home anchoring, accent-tolerant city search and a pin-drop map picker.

features.title: Rich details
features.body: AQI, UV index, a sun-path arc, wind compass and pressure gauge.

challenge: Outdoor temperature is a poor proxy for how a room actually feels. Sunlight, room size and an AC or heater can move the indoor reading by several degrees.
approach: A pure-Dart thermal model sits between the data layer and the UI. It takes outdoor conditions, sun exposure, room size and HVAC runtime as inputs, and Riverpod recomputes the estimate whenever any of them change.

title: First Aid Assistant
description: An offline-first, bilingual (English and Urdu) emergency guide with Urdu text-to-speech and a nearest-hospital locator, designed to stay clear and usable under stress.
headline: Emergency guidance that works with no signal.
overview: An emergency reference is useless if it needs a network. First Aid Assistant ships every protocol on-device, reads steps aloud in Urdu so hands stay free, and finds the nearest hospital from your location, all behind a high-contrast interface built to reduce cognitive load in a crisis.
architecture: Emergency protocols bundled as local JSON, so life-saving content never waits on a network
Riverpod providers expose language, theme and protocol state to the UI
Location services and an in-app browser view power the hospital locator

features.title: Offline-first
features.body: Every emergency protocol is stored and served on-device.

features.title: English & Urdu
features.body: Switch languages instantly, with Urdu rendered alongside English titles.

features.title: Urdu text-to-speech
features.body: Steps are read aloud so users can follow them hands-free.

features.title: Nearest hospital
features.body: Detects your location and maps nearby hospitals without leaving the app.

challenge: The app has to be dependable in exactly the moments when connectivity and attention are least reliable, while serving content in two languages and two scripts.
approach: All protocols ship with the app as local data, Urdu guidance is spoken through on-device text-to-speech, and a restrained clinical design system reserves emergency red for the actions that matter.

title: Note App
description: A cross-platform notes app with Firebase authentication and Cloud Firestore sync, built on a clean MVVM structure that keeps business logic out of the UI.
headline: A notes app built as an architecture exercise.
overview: Note App is a full-stack notes client with sign-up, login and password reset through Firebase Authentication, and notes stored in Cloud Firestore so they follow the user across devices. It was written to a strict MVVM structure, with ChangeNotifier view-models between the widgets and the backend.
architecture: View, ViewModel and Model layers kept strictly separate
Provider ChangeNotifiers own authentication and notes state
Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore as the backend

features.title: Authentication
features.body: Sign up, log in, log out and reset a forgotten password by email.

features.title: Notes CRUD
features.body: Create, edit and delete notes with a title and description.

features.title: Cloud sync
features.body: Notes live in Cloud Firestore and are available on any device.

features.title: Clean MVVM
features.body: Logic and UI stay in separate layers, so features are easy to extend.

challenge: Cloud backends make it easy to leak Firebase calls into widgets, which is what makes apps like this hard to extend later.
approach: ChangeNotifier view-models sit between Firebase and the screens, so widgets only talk to view-models and the data source can change without touching the UI.
